value: 31B Dense model: 30.7B parameters, 60 layers, 1024-token sliding window, 256K context, 262K vocabulary. Hybrid attention interleaves local sliding window attention with full global attention (final layer always global), giving the speed and low memory footprint of a lightweight model without sacrificing deep awareness for complex, long-context tasks. Global layers use unified Keys and Values and Proportional RoPE (p-RoPE) to optimize memory for long contexts.

value: The card acknowledges that VLMs trained on real-world data can reflect socio-cultural biases; mitigation consists of careful scrutiny, input data pre-processing, and post-training evaluations. Training data was filtered for CSAM, certain personal/sensitive data, and by content quality and safety. It also notes biases or gaps in training data can limit responses, and encourages continuous monitoring and exploration of de-biasing techniques.
quote: VLMs trained on large-scale, real-world text and image data can reflect socio-cultural biases embedded in the training material. Gemma 4 models underwent careful scrutiny, input data pre-processing, and post-training evaluations as reported in this card to help mitigate the risk of these biases. [...] **Perpetuation of biases**: It's encouraged to perform continuous monitoring (using evaluation metrics, human review) and the exploration of de-biasing techniques during model training, fine-tuning, and other use cases. [...] Filtering based on content quality and safety in line with [our policies](https://ai.google/static/documents/ai-responsibility-update-published-february-2025.pdf). [...] The quality and diversity of the training data significantly influence the model's capabilities. Biases or gaps in the training data can lead to limitations in the model's responses.

value: The card gives rationales for some design choices. Hybrid attention (local sliding window interleaved with global) gives the speed and low memory footprint of a lightweight model without losing deep awareness for long-context tasks. Training data includes code to learn programming syntax and patterns, and mathematical text to learn logical reasoning, symbolic representation and to address mathematical queries.
quote: This hybrid design delivers the processing speed and low memory footprint of a lightweight model without sacrificing the deep awareness required for complex, long-context tasks. [...] Exposing the model to code helps it to learn the syntax and patterns of programming languages, which improves its ability to generate code and understand code-related questions. [...] Training on mathematical text helps the model learn logical reasoning, symbolic representation, and to address mathematical queries.
quotes: This hybrid design delivers the processing speed and low memory footprint of a lightweight model without sacrificing the deep awareness required for complex, long-context tasks.
Exposing the model to code helps it to learn the syntax and patterns of programming languages, which improves its ability to generate code and understand code-related questions.
Training on mathematical text helps the model learn logical reasoning, symbolic representation, and to address mathematical queries.

value: Usable with the Hugging Face Transformers library (pip install -U transformers torch accelerate; load via AutoProcessor and AutoModelForMultimodalLM). Chat format uses system, assistant and user roles; thinking is enabled with the <|think|> token at the start of the system prompt.
quote: You can use all Gemma 4 models with the latest version of Transformers. To get started, install the necessary dependencies in your environment: [...] `pip install -U transformers torch accelerate` [...] from transformers import AutoProcessor, AutoModelForMultimodalLM [...] Compared to Gemma 3, the models use standard `system`, `assistant`, and `user` roles. To properly manage the thinking process, use the following control tokens: [...] **Trigger Thinking:** Thinking is enabled by including the `<|think|>` token at the start of the system prompt.
quotes: You can use all Gemma 4 models with the latest version of Transformers. To get started, install the necessary dependencies in your environment:
`pip install -U transformers torch accelerate`
from transformers import AutoProcessor, AutoModelForMultimodalLM
Compared to Gemma 3, the models use standard `system`, `assistant`, and `user` roles. To properly manage the thinking process, use the following control tokens:
**Trigger Thinking:** Thinking is enabled by including the `<|think|>` token at the start of the system prompt.

Automated and human evaluations were conducted with internal safety and responsible AI teams, aligned with Google's AI principles and safety policies. Results: major improvements in all content safety categories relative to previous Gemma models; Gemma 4 significantly outperforms Gemma 3 and 3n on safety while keeping unjustified refusals low; testing was conducted without safety filters; minimal policy violations for text-to-text and image-to-text across all model sizes.
quote: Gemma 4 models were developed in partnership with internal safety and responsible AI teams. A range of automated as well as human evaluations were conducted to help improve model safety. [...] For all areas of safety testing, we saw major improvements in all categories of content safety relative to previous Gemma models. Overall, Gemma 4 models significantly outperform Gemma 3 and 3n models in improving safety, while keeping unjustified refusals low. All testing was conducted without safety filters to evaluate the model capabilities and behaviors. [...] For both text-to-text and image-to-text, and across all model sizes, the model produced minimal policy violations, and showed significant improvements over previous Gemma models' performance.
quotes: Gemma 4 models were developed in partnership with internal safety and responsible AI teams. A range of automated as well as human evaluations were conducted to help improve model safety.

For all areas of safety testing, we saw major improvements in all categories of content safety relative to previous Gemma models. Overall, Gemma 4 models significantly outperform Gemma 3 and 3n models in improving safety, while keeping unjustified refusals low. All testing was conducted without safety filters to evaluate the model capabilities and behaviors.
For both text-to-text and image-to-text, and across all model sizes, the model produced minimal policy violations, and showed significant improvements over previous Gemma models' performance.
